history.issue: The final exclusive bound can equal an accepted cue's start, silently losing that cue or crashing segmentation. parse_json3 at line 39 defaults missing/null/zero duration to 0. If the final such cue starts at an exact second, end_s equals start_ms/1000 and _cut's strict comparison at line 50 excludes it. Observed: events at 0ms (duration 1000ms) and 180000ms (duration omitted) produce only 'first' in fixed mode. Constant embeddings also drop it. With an additional cue at 60000ms and vectors [[1,0],[1,0],[0,1]], the final gap equals end_s; trial[k+1] at line 90 raises IndexError. Current tests at test_captions.py:128 exercise a positive fractional duration and miss this parser-supported case.
history.fix: Ensure the final whole-second exclusive bound is strictly greater than every retained cue start (for example, include max(start_ms)+1ms when deriving the ceiling), and only consider gaps strictly inside the current outer bounds. Add regression tests for a final whole-second cue with missing/zero duration in fixed and embedding modes, including the final-gap topic-change case; assert every cue appears exactly once and no exception occurs.

original_review_notes: Scope: independent review of the exact two-file diff; no implementation or Git mutations. The only repository file created by this review is this JSON report.

Spec: 03-plan.md:490 defines T3 and its tuple return contract; 03-plan.md:30 adds single; 02-design.md:65 specifies the segmentation algorithm. Implementation matches the explicit T3 sample, but the observed data-loss/crash defect still requires correction.

Parsing: captions.py:30-40 strips short bracketed markers, normalizes whitespace, skips empty/missing-start events and sorts by (start_ms,end_ms), preserving input order for equal keys. Covered by test_captions.py:32,82,97.

Return/fallback: captions.py:60-78 implements empty/short/one-window single, None/raising embedder fixed, and wrong-shape/non-finite/zero-row-norm fixed. Tests at test_captions.py:65,72,78,102,122 assert methods and concrete output. A one-window long cue deliberately returns single per the plan.

Boundaries: captions.py:85-101 enforces min_s on depth-based splits and chooses deepest eligible interior boundaries, breaking ties by earlier time; without positive interior depth it uses fixed spacing. Fixed tails can be shorter than min_s as allowed by the specified fallback. The structured one-hour probe exercised recursive splitting; existing test_captions.py:58 covers only its fixed-spacing branch.

Determinism: captions.py:67 sorts window keys; line 88 sorts the set immediately, so set iteration cannot affect bounds. Lines 85 and 100 include time in their sort keys. Identical numeric inputs have a fixed reduction order; four-process hash-seed probes confirmed equal-depth selection and output. No claim of cross-platform floating-point bit identity is needed or made.

Cue assignment: captions.py:50,66 assigns by start time, so a crossing cue stays in its starting window/segment and a cue starting exactly on an interior boundary goes to the later one. Overlap does not duplicate cues. Positive-duration probes, including 450 randomized cases, conserved all cue labels. The terminal zero-duration exception is the finding above.

Empty windows: captions.py:64-67 omits unoccupied windows; parse_json3 line 37 filters blank cues, so normal parser output does not send empty strings to the embedder. Sparse-window probe observed only the four occupied window texts, with no lost cues.

Rounding: captions.py:63 rounds the final positive fractional end upward (181100ms becomes 182s); test_captions.py:128-141 explicitly requires this. This differs from the general floor wording at 02-design.md:71 but follows the more specific T3 plan implementation at 03-plan.md:653 and protects fractional terminal cues. All produced boundaries were integers.

Performance: captions.py:81 is O(n^2) in occupied windows, and _cut scans cues for each interval. At the specified 3600s/180-window scale, measured local segmentation stayed below 1.6ms in these probes, excluding embedder/network time. Recursive splits at lines 93-101 shrink by at least min_s on both sides, bounding the default one-hour path depth below roughly 81; observed depth was 3. No must-fix performance or recursion issue at the supported scale.

Test quality: concrete boundary, text, method and invalid-embedding assertions meaningfully exercise the new module and would not pass without its implementation. The missing essential regression is final missing/zero-duration cue retention and the associated end-boundary crash. Dedicated committed tests for competing equal-depth ties and positive-depth split_long would improve coverage; independent probes found no additional defect in those paths.
